summary: Mery Cecconi is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD candidate at Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.
Mettanando Bhikkhu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.
Mewa Khenpo Norbu Tendzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Michael Alram works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. His posts include positions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and vice presidency of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Durham University and the University of London under David Snellgrove. He held posts at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Harvard University.
Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library, attested in 1991.

Art historian Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) studied at Downing College, Cambridge, and the universities of Pavia and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, Warburg Institute, Courtauld Institute of Art, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the University of Bonn and at Heidelberg University under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty at the University of Washington as a professor from circa 1974 to 2017 and was named Professor Emeritus of Hindi around 2017.

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford. He held lectureships at Oxford and the London School of Economics before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, later serving as a faculty member at the University of Sydney (circa 1989–2002).
Michael J. Conway specializes in Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is attested in 2026 as faculty at the Otani Academic Society.

Michael Eido Luetchford (1944–2023) focused on Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an electronic engineering degree at the University of Bradford (~1964–1967) and studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima.

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich (~1976–1984), where he was an assistant from 1983 to 1986. He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael Hahn (1941–2014) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wilhelm Rau and earned his PhD at the University of Marburg, where he later held the Indology and Tibetology chair. He also held posts at the University of Bonn.
Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and sinology. Attested in 2007, he completed a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.

Michael Hutt works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his BA and doctorate at SOAS University of London and the University of London, later serving at SOAS as Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.

Michael I. Como specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and sinology, having studied under advisers Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He holds the position of Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University (attested 2009, 2026).

Michael J. Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his doctoral studies under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael Janda works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, habilitated at the University of Zurich, and was appointed to the Indo-European linguistics chair at the University of Münster in 2002.
